questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was interested in Japanese culture, nature and have a little bit of Japanese heritage. I wanted to live somewhere very different from Denmark but still a very safe place where I would be able to do solo traveling as a woman.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Waseda sent a lot of information that was quite overwhelming at first but there were also info meeting and these were also very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received assistance from Waseda University about how to apply for courses and they answered some questions I had about the application process and system.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Wasedas communication was very good and I received help quickly whenever I had questions. My uncertainty was more because of KU, who were much harder to communicate with regarding the exchange.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The university sent out a form with a lot of different dorms and share houses, so I only applied for some of these. The dorms both had cheaper and more expensive options (3500 - 5500 dkk/month).

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I chose a dorm specifically because of the meal plan, which meant my dorm didn't have great cooking facilities, but I heard that the dorms without meal plan had much better equipped kitchens.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I found it super convenient and nice to get to know a lot of other Waseda students. I chose one near the university and with a meal plan so it was more expensive, but it was also possible to find cheaper options close to Waseda.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of the dorms have very strict rules about visitors and gender separation, which feels weird coming from a Danish context.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The course registration happens in 3 periods, so you first choose your top priorities, and then you can apply for new courses in the second and third registration. This process was quite confusing and it was hard for me to get the schedule I wanted because I couldn't apply for two courses in the same time period in case I didn't get one - then in the second period my plan b was full, so I had to choose something completely different.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The SILS office was very helpful, but the system is very rigid and there is not much to do about it.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In the end I got 6/7 courses that I wanted,

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: In the first registration, apply for as many of the courses you want as possible, because I didn't get quite a few of mine.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Generally, the courses were easier in terms of what was needed to pass.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There is more focus on attendance, participation and multiple courses with presentations.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: State and Society in the Middle East, Thinking Power, The Politics and International Relations of the European Union, Nihongo 1 and Zero Japanese

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
State and Society in the Middle East was my favorite course because the teacher was an expert and made the class very lively. It was also very easy with almost no readings, and I appreciated the time to explore Japan. 
Zero Japanese is a bit hardcore but in combination with Nihongo 1, it worked very well for me for learning basic Japanese. They are both for beginners though I would heavily recommend knowing hiragana at least before starting (I did with duolingo).

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I was a bit surprised at how many housing fees there are. This makes it hard to calculate your monthly rent, as the fees could be as high as almost 2 months rent (for my 5 month stay).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out is very cheap but vegetables and fruits in grocery stores are not. It is very difficult/expensive to be vegetarian.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are hundreds of circles to join for sports, arts and gatherings.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed sports, because it was fun and easy to make friends with people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are lots of great trips (day trips also) from Tokyo such as Nikko, Kamakura, Enoshima, Yokohama. I loved traveling and going to flea markets

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy - I am quiet and polite as a person so the Japanese culture didn't feel too different.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Almost all my Japanese friends are people I met in my dorm (at dinner). Otherwise I would say to be open and to initiate conversations, because many Japanese people can seem very shy, but a lot of the time they will enjoy speaking to you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language/cultural barrier with my Japanese friends made it hard for me to know whether we were friends in the beginning, because they don't share as much about their personal lives.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The politeness and respect for other people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Hmmmmm...
1. To think carefully about which living situation to apply for: Do you want to make friends there? Do you want it to be cheap? How convenient do you want it to be?
2. Talk to your friends/peers at Waseda, cause they can in most cases point you in the right direction and make you feel like you're not alone with any issues you may be having
3. ?

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared for an annoying course registration system...

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My friends made it very memorable.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Communication with KU

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
